en: Hello everyone, and welcome to the new episode of the podcast “Zman Ivrit” (“Time for Hebrew”).

If you’ve been listening to this podcast long enough, you may remember that not long ago, in episode 103, I talked about Ashkenazim and Mizrahim. Ashkenazim are Jews who came to Israel from Europe. Mizrahim are Jews who came to Israel from the Middle East and North Africa.

When I talked about Mizrahim and Ashkenazim, I said that there are also Jews who came to Israel from the Soviet Union. “The Soviet Union” in English is—and in Russian, what I said then was that these Jews who came from the Soviet Union are not exactly Ashkenazim. And that maybe in the future I’ll make a separate episode about them.

Why aren’t Jews from the Soviet Union exactly Ashkenazi? Because as I told you then, Ashkenazim and Mizrahim are not only geographical categories. That is, they’re not connected only to the place people came to Israel from. They’re also sociological categories. When we talk about Ashkenazim and Mizrahim in Israel, usually we’re talking about different sociological groups. So immigrants from the Soviet Union are simply a separate sociological group. They’re not exactly Ashkenazi.
So that’s what I want to talk about in this episode: immigration to Israel from the Soviet Union and the lives of those immigrants in Israel.

Now, if you’ve been listening to this podcast long enough, you know that I myself came to Israel from Russia. So of course this topic is very close to me personally. That’s why, in the last part of the episode, I’ll also tell you a few stories related to my family, which immigrated to Israel from Russia. Okay. Ready? Let’s begin!
Okay. So in this part, I want to talk a little about the lives of Jews in the Soviet Union after World War II. That is, in the period before immigration to Israel.

During that period, the Jewish community in the Soviet Union was one of the largest Jewish communities in the world. Around three million Jews lived there. But the lives of Jews in the Soviet Union at that time were anything but easy. One of the main reasons for that was antisemitism. Jews experienced antisemitism everywhere: at school, at university, at work...

At school, children experienced harassment from other children and sometimes even from teachers. At university, it was harder for Jews than for others to be admitted. Especially to prestigious faculties like medicine or mathematics. And at work, it was harder for Jews than for others to advance and succeed in their profession. In short, being Jewish in the Soviet Union was not especially pleasant or socially positive. It was basically like being in a lower status than others. So Jews in the Soviet Union always tried to be really good at everything they did. Because Jews knew they had to be better than others, even much better than others, in order to succeed in life.
In the Soviet Union overall, there was a culture of academic excellence. Being excellent at school and then at university was seen as a key to success in life. So for Jews that was also
the case, but even more so.

Up to now, I’ve talked about Jews in the Soviet Union. But in fact, it’s important to understand that in the Soviet Union at that time there wasn’t really Jewish life as we usually think of it. What do I mean? First of all, because of antisemitism, many Jews simply tried to hide the fact that they were Jews. The word “to hide” means “not to show,” “to conceal.” Of course that wasn’t easy. Jews could be identified fairly easily by the way they looked, by their names, or by their identity cards. But many Jews did try to hide the fact that they were Jews and be as much like everyone else as possible.

Besides that, as you probably know, the Soviet Union was under communist rule. Communist rule was against religion in general, and from everything I’ve told you so far, you can understand that it was especially against Judaism. So even Jews who didn’t want to hide the fact that they were Jews, and who did want to live Jewish lives, found it extremely difficult to do so. Almost impossible. Celebrating Jewish holidays or learning Hebrew was really dangerous. Anyone who did that could find themselves under KGB interrogation, be fired from their job, or even be sent to prison or a labor camp.

Therefore, after many years of communist rule, Jews in the Soviet Union were a bit of an unusual kind of Jews. On the one hand, they knew very well that they were Jews. Because everyone was always reminding them that they were Jews: at school, at university, at work... But on the other hand, many of them didn’t really know Jewish tradition. As I said before, their lives פשוט just weren’t Jewish lives as we usually think of them.

From everything I’ve told you so far, you can understand that being Jewish in the Soviet Union was not simple at all. The thing is that at that time, leaving the Soviet Union wasn’t simple either. You couldn’t just say, “Okay, I’m not happy here. I’m moving somewhere else!” In fact, to emigrate from the Soviet Union, you had to get special permission from the state. Getting that permission was hard
very hard. It was a long process and required lots of documents. And at the end of that process, most of the people who applied for permission didn’t get it.

But little by little, things changed. In the early 1970s, the Soviet Union decided to allow Jews to leave more freely. Not completely freely, but more freely. During that period, quite a few Jews left the Soviet Union and immigrated to Israel. About 150,000 Jews.

Later, in the mid-1980s, all kinds of major reforms began in the Soviet Union. Some of those reforms allowed Jews to leave even more freely. Even then, quite a few Jews decided to do so and immigrate to Israel.

But the real big change came in the early 1990s. As you all probably know, in the early 1990s the Soviet Union collapsed. After that happened, huge numbers of Jews left the Soviet Union. And most of them immigrated to Israel.

So in the early 1990s, and really throughout the whole 1990s, huge numbers of Jews immigrated from the Soviet Union to Israel. Huge, huge numbers. How many exactly? By the year 2000, there were already one million immigrants from the Soviet Union in Israel. One million! To understand how big that immigration was, you need to understand that at that time only four million people lived in Israel in total. That is, after this immigration, Israel’s population grew by a quarter: four million plus one million. So it was truly enormous. And in fact, when we talk today about immigration from the Soviet Union to Israel, we’re mostly talking about this wave in the 1990s.

Okay. Remember that in the previous part I talked about how there was a culture of excellence in the Soviet Union? And that this was especially true for Jews? So as you can imagine, among the one million new immigrants
who came to Israel, there were many very talented people. For example, doctors, scientists, engineers, people in culture, athletes, and so on and so on.
That’s why today in Israel you can see many Russian speakers in medicine, science, hi-tech, culture, sports, and of course in many other fields as well.

So there’s no doubt that immigration from the Soviet Union was very good for Israel. It helped Israel a lot to become the successful country it is today. And overall, you could say it was good for many of the immigrants themselves too. For all the reasons I talked about in the previous part.

But the story of immigration from the Soviet Union is not only a good and happy story. For many new immigrants from the Soviet Union, this immigration was difficult and complicated. So in this part and in the next one, I want to focus on the difficulties and complexities of this immigration.

In an ideal situation, when new immigrants arrive in Israel, they go to an absorption center. They stay in the absorption center for about half a year, maybe even a year. During that time they get a small apartment that costs very little, or nothing at all. And in everyday life, what they mainly do is go to ulpan and learn Hebrew.

Basically, the purpose of the absorption center is to give immigrants time to settle into the country. That is, time to get used to life in the country and learn Hebrew. After new immigrants leave the absorption center, they begin to live ordinary lives. They go and find their own apartment, their own job, and so on and so on.

This idea of an absorption center is of course good for new immigrants. But as you can imagine, when so many new immigrants arrived in Israel in the wave from the Soviet Union, there wasn’t really room for everyone, or even for most of them, in the absorption centers. So most of the new immigrants from the Soviet Union did not go to an absorption center. In fact, they had to start living completely ordinary lives from the very first moment in Israel. These immigrants did receive some financial help from the state. That is, a certain amount of money that was supposed to help them start their lives in Israel. But you couldn’t really live on that money alone. To pay for an apartment and food and all the basic things needed for living, they had to find work from the very first moment in Israel.

Earlier I said that many educated people came in this wave. For example, doctors. In an ideal situation, a doctor would want to find work in Israel as... a doctor. But Israel is a small country. And there were already quite a few Israeli doctors there. So when, all at once, huge numbers of doctors from the Soviet Union suddenly arrived, of course it was very hard for most of them to find work as doctors.

Besides that, when they first arrived in Israel, of course most of these doctors didn’t know Hebrew at all. And as you can imagine, it’s not easy to find work in Israel as a doctor if you don’t know Hebrew. Of course the case of doctors is only one example. I hope you understand that I’m not only talking about doctors here, but also about many other professions.

So what happened was that many such new immigrants couldn’t find work in their profession. Therefore, they had to start working in the most basic jobs available. Many people who in the Soviet Union had been doctors or engineers or musicians became street cleaners, security guards in malls, cashiers in supermarkets, and so on and so on.
And that’s pretty sad. These people worked very hard all their lives to be excellent in their profession, but when they arrived in Israel all of that simply counted for nothing.

Another thing I want to talk about is the difficulty many immigrants from the Soviet Union had in integrating into Israeli society. Finding work is of course part of the issue. But that’s not the whole issue. Integrating into society is also a matter of culture and language. Now, as you can imagine, Soviet culture is quite different from Israeli culture. And as all of you know very well, Hebrew is not an easy language at all. So many immigrants from the Soviet Union found it hard to integrate into Israeli society. It was hard for them to get used to Israeli culture, and it was hard for them to learn Hebrew.

In fact, when immigrants from the Soviet Union arrived in the country, they had to choose a place to live. And of course many of them preferred to live where other immigrants like them were already living. That led to a situation where many immigrants from the Soviet Union ended up in the same places. Today, in cities like Ashdod, Bat Yam, Haifa, and various other cities, there are huge numbers of immigrants from the Soviet Union. Huge numbers. So certain places in these cities have a somewhat Soviet character. Almost everywhere you can see signs in Russian and hear people speaking Russian.

Not long ago, one of my students went on a trip to Haifa. This student is a young man who immigrated to Israel from Belarus, and today he lives in Tel Aviv. When he came back from the trip, he told me that in various places in Haifa he really felt as if he had arrived in Russia of the 1980s. As if he’d stepped into a time machine and landed in the old Soviet world.

Now, on the one hand, of course that’s nice. Because immigrants from the Soviet Union didn’t have to give up completely on the Soviet world they came from. But on the other hand, think about it. Think about an older Soviet person who already finds it hard to integrate into Israeli society and learn Hebrew. And who can basically avoid meeting Hebrew-speaking Israelis for most of their life. Does that help this person integrate into Israeli society and learn Hebrew, or does it actually make it harder? Of course it makes it harder. And that’s a problem.

Besides that, since the 1990s, quite a bit of Russian-language culture has started to develop in Israel. Russian-language TV channels and radio stations were opened, Russian bookstores were established, Russian theaters were established, and so on and so on. What’s important to understand here is that the immigrants from the Soviet Union loved Soviet culture, Russian-language culture. They didn’t want to leave that culture behind when they arrived in Israel. They wanted to keep speaking Russian and reading Russian and hearing the news in Russian and watching theater performances in Russian.

And here too, on the one hand that’s great. The Russian-language culture that developed in Israel is a very special and very interesting culture. But on the other hand, we come back to the same question we asked before. When there is Russian radio and Russian television in Israel, does that encourage new immigrants to learn Hebrew, or quite the opposite?

In short, for many immigrants from the Soviet Union it was hard to integrate into Israeli society and learn Hebrew. Many of them basically continued living their lives through the Russian language. And I think this is really a kind of circle: many people continued living through the Russian language because it was hard for them to integrate in Israel, and it was hard for them to integrate in Israel because they continued living through the Russian language.
Okay. In this part I want to tell you less about immigration from the Soviet Union in general, and more stories from the lives of my relatives and from my own life.
So among the immigrants in the big wave of the 1990s were also my aunt, her husband, and their two children. Their children were still quite young: one was two years old and the other was 10.
In the Soviet Union, my aunt’s husband was a doctor. And my aunt was a French teacher.

When they arrived in the country, they got a small amount of financial help from the state. But that money wasn’t really enough for them to rent their own apartment. So at first they lived with friends in a very old and very small apartment in Bat Yam. Bat Yam is a small city near Tel Aviv.

My aunt’s husband looked for work as a doctor. But it was not easy at all to find such a job. Mainly because he still didn’t know Hebrew. At first, he found work as a kind of paramedic. And it was a night-shift job. So basically, he would work at night and sleep in the morning. In his free time, in the afternoon, he would learn Hebrew and look for another job, a better job.

Pretty quickly he managed to learn enough Hebrew and also found a better job, as a doctor in a health maintenance organization. Over time, they also managed to buy their own apartment in Holon. Holon is another small city near Bat Yam and Tel Aviv. That apartment in Holon was already quite nice, and most importantly, it was theirs. They no longer had to live with other people.

My aunt, as I already said, was a French teacher. And it was harder for her to find work than for her husband. She couldn’t try to find work as a schoolteacher in Israel, because she didn’t know Hebrew. And she also couldn’t really give private lessons. Because most of the Russian speakers around her
didn’t have money for private lessons. And of course she couldn’t teach Israelis because, as I already said, she didn’t know Hebrew.
In the end she found work in a Russian-language theater. And she stayed there for many years.

My aunt’s husband worked with Israelis. So of course over time he learned Hebrew better and better. Today, of course, he understands Hebrew well and speaks it well. But my aunt worked mainly with Russian speakers. So she never really learned Hebrew at a high level. Today, even after more than 30 years in Israel, she still doesn’t know Hebrew very well.

My aunt and her husband, like many other immigrants from the Soviet Union, spoke only Russian at home. Both with each other and with their children. So their children grew up with Russian culture and the Russian language. But on the other hand, those children grew up in Israel. They went to school in Israel, they enlisted in the army in Israel, and so on and so on. So they also grew up with Israeli culture and the Hebrew language.

hebrew_paragraphs: שלום לכולם ולכולן, וברוכים הבאים לפרק החדש של הפודקאסט "זמן עברית". אם אתם מקשיבים לפודקאסט הזה מספיק זמן, אתם יודעים שמדי פעם אני ובעלי נוסעים לאירופה ונשארים שם לתקופה מסוימת: חודש, חודשיים, לפעמים אפילו שלושה חודשים.

בעצם, אנחנו משכירים את הדירה שלנו בירושלים לתקופה הזאת, זאת אומרת, עושים סאבלט לדירה שלנו, ובכסף של הסאבלט הזה אנחנו שוכרים דירה אחרת במקום שאליו אנחנו נוסעים. בכמה פרקים בעבר, סיפרתי לכם על נסיעות כאלה: לברלין, לבוקרשט, לבודפשט, וכן הלאה וכן הלאה.

השנה, בסוף ינואר, אני ובעלי נסענו לשני מקומות: לסינייה, שהיא עיר קטנה ברומניה, ולבודפשט, שהיא עיר הבירה של הונגריה. בסינייה היינו בערך שבוע, ובבודפשט היינו בערך חודשיים. זאת הייתה תקופה מעניינת, ועל זה אני בעצם רוצה לספר לכם בפרק הזה.
אוקיי. מוכנים? בואו נתחיל!
אוקיי. אז בסוף ינואר השנה, אני ובעלי טסנו לרומניה. טסנו לבוקרשט, ומשם לקחנו רכבת לסינייה.

סינייה היא עיר קטנה שנמצאת בערך שעה וחצי נסיעה ברכבת מבוקרשט. זאת עיר שאין בה הרבה מה לעשות, אבל היא נמצאת באזור מאוד יפה עם הרבה הרים גבוהים והרבה שלג. אז בעצם, רוב מי שמגיע לסינייה בחורף מגיע אליה כדי לעשות סקי בהרים המושלגים שלה. וזאת גם הסיבה שאנחנו הגענו לסינייה: לעשות סקי. אבל זאת לא הסיבה העיקרית שבגללה הגענו לסינייה.

לא מזמן, בן דוד שלי ואשתו החליטו שהם עוזבים את ישראל ועוברים לגור ב... סינייה. זה היה דבר שמאוד הפתיע את כל המשפחה. הם בעצם קנו בסינייה בית גדול, עם כמה קומות והרבה חדרים, והחליטו להפוך את הבית הזה לסוג של מלון בוטיק. הם בעצם החליטו שהם רוצים לגור בסינייה ולעבוד בלנהל את המלון הזה. אז מאז שזה קרה, הם נמצאים בסינייה, משפצים את הבית הזה ומנסים להקים את המלון שלהם.

כמובן שמאז שכל זה קרה, אני וקרובי המשפחה שלי רצינו לנסוע לסינייה ולבקר אותם. גם כדי לראות אותם וגם כדי לראות את הבית שלהם ואת המלון שהם בונים. הזמן שהכי התאים לכולם היה ינואר השנה. ובגלל שינואר זאת תקופה שבה אפשר לעשות סקי, החלטנו שהביקור הזה יהיה גם חופשת סקי. אגב, אם כל פעם שאני אומרת את השם "סינייה" אתם חושבים לעצמכם שזה מאוד דומה ל"סיני," כמו הר סיני, המקום שבו עם ישראל קיבל את התורה, אז אתם צודקים. סינייה באמת נקראת על שם הר סיני.

בכל מקרה, בסוף ינואר אני ובעלי טסנו לרומניה, וכשהגענו לסינייה פגשנו את קרובי המשפחה שלי. הם כבר שכרו וילה גדולה שבה כולנו יכלנו לגור יחד, ואנחנו הצטרפנו אליהם. בהתחלה, חשבנו שכולנו נישן בבית של בן דוד שלי ואשתו. אבל הבית הזה עדיין היה בשיפוצים. לכן שכרנו בית
גדול משלנו לשבוע, ותכננו להיפגש איתם כמה פעמים במהלך השבוע הזה. וחוץ מזה, התכנית הייתה בכל בוקר לקום וללכת לעשות סקי.

אני כבר יודעת לעשות סקי. בשנה שעברה, הייתי בחופשת סקי בשוודיה עם חברה משוודיה. ובתור ילדה עשיתי סקי לא מעט פעמים, אבל לא בהרים אלא במישור. גם קרובי המשפחה שלי כבר יודעים לעשות סקי. הם נוסעים לחופשות סקי מדי פעם. אבל בעלי אף פעם לא עשה סקי. אז חשבנו שזאת הזדמנות טובה בשבילו לנסות וללמוד. והוא הסכים לנסות וללמוד. אבל... האמת היא שהוא לא מאוד אהב את זה.

כדי לעשות סקי, צריך לקום מוקדם בבוקר. צריך לקחת את כל ציוד הסקי הכבד ולעלות להר לאתר הסקי. ואז פשוט לגלוש בשלג ממקום אחד למקום אחר. וכשכל זה נגמר, אחרי כמה שעות, מרגישים עייפים. גם בגלל שמתחילים מוקדם בבוקר וגם בגלל שלגלוש בשלג זה מעייף. זה קשה פיזית, בעיקר בהתחלה. אז פשוט חוזרים הביתה בצהריים ונחים עד הערב.

בעלי חשב שכל זה פשוט בזבוז של זמן. זה נראה לו לא כל כך הגיוני שהאנרגיה של כל היום מתבזבזת על לעלות להר ולגלוש בשלג ממקום אחד למקום אחר. בקיצור, הוא חשב שכל הפעילות הזאת היא מיותרת. והוא לא כל-כך רצה להמשיך לבוא איתנו לעשות סקי אחרי היום הראשון.

אבל אני מקווה שאתם זוכרים שהמטרה העיקרית של הנסיעה הזאת לא הייתה לעשות סקי וגם לא לבקר בטירת פלש, אלא לבקר את בן דוד שלי ואשתו. האמת היא שיצא לנו לפגוש אותם הרבה פחות ממה שרצינו במהלך השבוע הזה. אבל באחד הימים האחרונים שלנו בסינייה כן הלכנו לארוחת ערב בבית שלהם. וזה היה מאוד נחמד להתארח אצלם.

הבית שלהם בעצם נמצא על הר. מצד אחד של הבית יש יער, ומהצד השני יש נוף מאוד יפה של הרים מושלגים. האמת היא שלהגיד על הנוף הזה שהוא מאוד יפה זה כמעט לא להגיד כלום. זה נוף פשוט מדהים. ובעצם, בכל קומה של הבית יש חלונות שמהם אפשר לראות את הנוף. החלון הכי טוב הוא החלון בסלון של הבית שנמצא בקומה האמצעית. זה חלון ענק, בגודל של כל הקיר כמעט, ומולו יש פינת ישיבה ושולחן קפה. בן דוד שלי ואשתו אומרים שכל בוקר הם מתחילים את היום שלהם בפינת הישיבה הזאת. אז זה היה ערב מאוד נחמד. ישבנו בסלון שלהם, אכלנו ושתינו ודיברנו. בן דוד שלי סיפר לנו סיפורים על החיים בסינייה, על ההבדלים בין רומניה לישראל, על איך הם מסתדרים בסינייה בלי לדעת רומנית, וכן הלאה וכן הלאה. זה באמת היה ערב מאוד נחמד.

כמו שכבר אמרתי, חלק מהבית עדיין נמצא בשיפוצים. והמלון אמור להיפתח רק בעוד כמה חודשים. אז אני מקווה שבעתיד הקרוב יצא לנו לחזור לסינייה ולבקר אותם שוב כשהבית הזה כבר יהפוך למלון אמיתי.

אוקיי. אז בתחילת פברואר השבוע שלנו בסינייה נגמר. חלק מקרובי המשפחה שלי החליטו להישאר בסינייה לעוד שבוע. חלק מקרובי המשפחה שלי טסו למקום אחר. ואני ובעלי טסנו לבודפשט. אם אתם מקשיבים לפודקאסט הזה מספיק זמן, אתם אולי זוכרים שגם בשנה שעברה אני ובעלי היינו בבודפשט. באותה התקופה פחות או יותר. מסוף ינואר עד תחילת מרץ. סיפרתי לכם על זה בפרק 92. בכל מקרה, בשנה שעברה מאוד נהנינו בבודפשט. זאת עיר מאוד יפה, לא יקרה, ודי הופתענו מכמה שהחורף שם היה נעים. זאת אומרת לא קר יחסית למקומות אחרים באירופה. השנה הגענו לבודפשט מסינייה. ובסינייה מאוד קר. אז ממש הרגשנו הקלה כשהגענו לבודפשט.

בשנה שעברה בבודפשט, שכרנו דירה יחסית רחוק ממרכז העיר. ואני חשבתי שזה דווקא היה יכול להיות נחמד לגור קרוב יותר למרכז העיר. אז הפעם מצאנו דירה שנמצאת ממש במרכז העיר. ואני חשבתי שזה מצוין.

הדירה עצמה הייתה בסך-הכל נחמדה מאוד. וכמובן שמאוד נהנינו מהמיקום המצוין שלה. אבל היה דבר אחד שהיה מאוד מוזר: הבניין.

הבניין היה גדול וישן. מהבניינים הגדולים והישנים שיש בהרבה ערים באירופה. עם דלת כניסה ענקית, מדרגות רחבות, וכן הלאה וכן הלאה.

הדבר הראשון שהיה מוזר בבניין הזה היה הריח. תמיד היה בו ריח של עישון. זאת אומרת ריח של סיגריות. בפעם הראשונה שנכנסנו לבניין, מאוד הופתענו מהריח. ואז כשעלינו במדרגות ראינו שכל הבניין מלא בשלטים שאומרים שאסור לעשן. עכשיו, זה מצחיק. כי אף פעם לא יצא לי לראות שלטים שאומרים שאסור לעשן בתוך בניין מגורים. חשבתי שזה פשוט מובן מאליו שלא עושים את זה. ואף פעם לא יצא להריח ריח כל-כך חזק של סיגריות בתוך בניין מגורים. שוב, חשבתי שזה מובן

מאליו שפשוט לא עושים את זה. אז כאן היו שלטים שאומרים שאסור לעשן וגם ריח ממש חזק של עישון.

אני ובעלי חשבנו שזה די מצחיק. ואחרי כמה ימים אמרנו שלהיכנס לבניין הזה זה קצת כמו להיכנס לתוך מאפרה. מאפרה זה כלי שלתוכו מנערים את האפר של הסיגריה. באנגלית זה וברוסית אז מאז, אנחנו קוראים לבניין הזה "בניין המאפרה".

עוד דבר שהיה מוזר בבניין הזה היה הדיירים. זאת אומרת האנשים שגרים בבניין. בעצם, בכל החודש שהיינו שם, כמעט לא ראינו את האנשים שגרים שם. לא כל-כך ידענו מי השכנים שלנו. כשכן ראינו אנשים, אלה היו אנשים מאוד שונים. מדי פעם, ראינו אנשים שנראו כמו סטודנטים זרים. זאת אומרת סטודנטים שהגיעו לבודפשט ממדינה אחרת. אז חשבנו שיכול להיות שחלק מהבניין הזה הוא סוג של מגורים לסטודנטים זרים. בפעמים אחרות, ראינו אנשים שנראו מאוד מוזנחים. זאת אומרת עם בגדים מלוכלכים ושיער מבולגן. אז חשבנו שיכול להיות שבמקום הזה יש סוג של מרכז גמילה מסמים או מאלכוהול. או אולי דירות סוציאליות לאנשים שנמצאים בגמילה.

חוץ מזה, האנשים שגרו בדירה מעלינו היו משוגעים לגמרי. בכל לילה, בסביבות 12:00 או 1:00 בלילה, הייתה מתחילה להתנגן מוזיקת מסיבות ממש חזקה בדירה שלהם. וזה באמת נשמע כאילו הייתה שם מסיבה. כל לילה. לפעמים גם בבוקר או בצהריים המוזיקה הזאת הייתה מתחילה להתנגן. ואני באמת לא יודעת לאיזה אנשים יש זמן או כח למסיבה כל לילה או סתם באמצע היום.

האמת היא שעד הסוף לא באמת גילינו מה הסיפור של הבניין הזה. כמו שאמרתי, היום אנחנו פשוט קוראים לו "בניין המאפרה".

בתחילת מרץ, היינו אמורים לעזוב את הדירה הזאת ולחזור לישראל. אבל כמו שכולכם בטח זוכרים, בסוף פברואר התחילה מלחמה בין ישראל לאיראן. כמעט כל הטיסות בוטלו והיה מאוד קשה לחזור לארץ. לא בלתי אפשרי, אבל מאוד קשה. אולי אתם זוכרים שסיפרתי לכם על זה בפרק 109.

בכל מקרה, אנחנו התלבטנו אם לנסות לחזור. ובסוף החלטנו שהדבר הכי טוב בשבילנו יהיה לשכור דירה בבודפשט לעוד חודש. זאת אומרת עד תחילת אפריל. חשבנו שבתחילת אפריל דברים יירגעו וכבר יהיה יותר פשוט לחזור לארץ. בהתחלה, חשבנו להישאר באותה דירה. זאת אומרת בבניין המאפרה. אבל אז החלטנו בכל זאת לנסות לראות אם יש אפשרויות אחרות. ובאמת מצאנו דירה מצוינת שהייתה פנויה בדיוק בתאריכים שהיינו צריכים. מתחילת מרץ עד תחילת אפריל. אנחנו חשבנו שזה מאוד מוזר שהדירה הייתה פנויה בדיוק לתאריכים שאנחנו צריכים. כי היא הייתה תפוסה בכל התאריכים שלפני ובכל התאריכים שאחרי. ודווקא בחודש שהיינו צריכים, מתחילת מרץ עד תחילת אפריל, היא הייתה פנויה לגמרי. מוזר, לא? כשהגענו לדירה החדשה, ופגשנו את בעל הדירה, הוא הסביר לנו שהוא לא משכיר את הדירה לתקופות של פחות משלושה שבועות. כי הוא לא רוצה דיירים שבאים ליום-יומיים ועושים רעש ובלאגן. הוא רוצה אנשים רגועים שבאים לתקופה ארוכה כדי פשוט לחיות חיים רגילים.

כי בעצם כל האזור הזה הוא לא אזור מאוד תיירותי, והבניין הזה הוא בניין שיש בו לא מעט משפחות עם ילדים. אז הוא רוצה רק אנשים רגועים שהוא יודע שלא יעשו רעש ובלאגן. וכשהוא אמר את זה, חשבנו לעצמנו "אההה... בגלל זה הדירה הייתה פנויה לכל החודש".!

אז כמובן שהבניין הזה היה יותר נחמד מבניין המאפרה. וגם הדירה עצמה הייתה יותר נחמדה מהדירה הקודמת.

אוקיי. בחלק הזה אני רוצה לספר לכם על עוד שני דברים מעניינים שקרו לי בבודפשט. הדבר הראשון שאני רוצה לספר קשור לקיר טיפוס. כמו שחלקכם אולי זוכרים, באחד הפרקים האחרונים, פרק 106, סיפרתי לכם שלא מזמן התחלתי לטפס על קיר. טיפוס על קיר זה בעצם סוג של

ספורט. הולכים למקום שיש בו קיר מיוחד שנקרא קיר טיפוס. קיר טיפוס זה קיר שיש עליו כל מיני בליטות צבעוניות כאלה, ועל הקיר הזה מטפסים. באנגלית טיפוס על קיר זה וברוסית התחלתי לטפס על קיר מכמה סיבות. קודם כל, רציתי להתחיל לעשות סוג כלשהו של ספורט באופן קבוע. וזה נראה לי כמו משהו נחמד. חוץ מזה, חשבתי שזאת גם יכולה להיות הזדמנות טובה להכיר אנשים חדשים. כי הרבה אנשים מגיעים באופן קבוע לקיר הטיפוס, ואנשים שמגיעים באופן קבוע לומדים להכיר אחד השני.

וגם, כמעט בכל עיר גדולה בעולם יש קיר טיפוס. וזה מצוין. כי היה לי חשוב שהספורט שאני מתחילה לעשות יהיה ספורט שאני אוכל להמשיך לעשות בלי בעיה גם כשאני נוסעת לחו"ל. חוץ מזה, תמיד רציתי שתהיה לי אפשרות להכיר אנשים חדשים במקומות שבהם אני נמצאת בחו"ל. וזאת נראתה לי כמו דרך טובה לעשות את זה.

כבר ביום הראשון או השני בבודפשט מצאתי בפייסבוק מודעה על קבוצה שנפגשת בקיר טיפוס כדי לטפס יחד. ואני חשבתי שזה מושלם והלכתי.

הקבוצה הייתה ממש נחמדה. בעצם, כמעט כולם בקבוצה היו אנשים שהם לא בדיוק הונגרים, אלא הגיעו לבודפשט מכל מיני סיבות. המדריך של הקבוצה היה בחור צעיר מסוריה שהיגר לבודפשט לפני כמה שנים. הייתה שם בחורה מסלובקיה שהגיעה לבודפשט בשביל עבודה. היה בחור מאזרבייג'אן. היה בחור מטורקיה. וכן הלאה וכן הלאה.

חוץ מזה, היה שם בחור שעבד בקופה. הוא זה שבעצם מכר לי את הכרטיס בכניסה. ומאוחר יותר הוא הגיע לטפס בעצמו. התחלנו לדבר, וגיליתי שהוא בעצם בחור יהודי רוסי. הוא נולד במוסקבה ועבר להונגריה לפני בערך עשר שנים. דיברנו ברוסית ונוצר בינינו קשר טוב. לכן החלפנו מספרי

טלפון, ובחודשיים הבאים הלכנו לטפס ביחד עוד כמה פעמים. כשאני אהיה שוב בבודפשט, אולי בקיץ הקרוב, אני בטוח אצור איתו קשר שוב כדי שנלך לטפס ביחד.

וגם, לפני בערך שנה וחצי, מאזינה של הפודקאסט שלחה לי מייל וסיפרה לי קצת על עצמה. היא מורה לעברית שגרה בהונגריה. בפעם שעברה שהייתי בבודפשט, בשנה שעברה, נפגשנו לקפה. אבל לא יצא לנו להיפגש יותר מזה. הפעם כן יצא לנו להיפגש לא מעט פעמים. למה? כי הלכנו לטפס יחד.

אז אני מאוד שמחה על כל זה, כי זה בדיוק מה שרציתי כשהתחלתי עם כל העניין הזה של טיפוס קירות. רציתי ספורט שיהיה לי כיף לעשות, שאני אוכל לעשות אותו גם בחו"ל, ושיהיה לו גם אספקט חברתי. זאת אומרת שהוא יעזור לי להכיר אנשים חדשים ולשמור איתם על קשר. זה בדיוק מה שקרה, ולכן אני מאוד שמחה.

אוקיי. הדבר השני שאני רוצה לספר לכם קשור לבחירות. אם אתם עוקבים אחרי חדשות מהעולם, אתם כנראה יודעים שלא מזמן היו בחירות בהונגריה. הבחירות האלה היו בתחילת אפריל. ובגלל המלחמה בין ישראל לאיראן, בתחילת אפריל אנחנו עדיין היינו בבודפשט. אז בעצם יצא שהיינו בבודפשט תקופה ארוכה לפני הבחירות, בערך חודשיים, וגם בזמן הבחירות עצמן. וזה היה מאוד מעניין להסתכל על כל זה מהצד.

הבחירות האלה היו מאוד חשובות. מצד אחד היה ויקטור אורבן, שהוא ראש הממשלה כבר המון שנים. הוא הפך את הונגריה למדינה שמתנגדת לאיחוד האירופי, למרות שהיא עדיין חלק ממנו. מהצד השני היה פטר מג'יאר, שרצה להחזיר את הונגריה להיות מדינה שתומכת באיחוד האירופי.

אחד הדברים המפורסמים לגבי אורבן זה שהוא החליש מאוד את הדמוקרטיה בהונגריה. הוא עשה כל מיני רפורמות במערכת המשפט, בתקשורת, בשיטת הבחירות, וכן הלאה וכן הלאה. כל הדברים גרמו לזה שהיה מאוד קשה לנצח אותו בבחירות. לא בלתי אפשרי, אבל מאוד קשה. כבר הרבה

שנים שאורבן והמפלגה שלו הופכים להיות פחות ופחות פופולריים בהונגריה. ועדיין, קשה מאוד לנצח את אורבן בבחירות. אבל הפעם הייתה תחושה שונה. פטר מג'יאר הוביל בכל הסקרים ונראה שיש לו סיכוי לא רע בכלל לנצח. לפני כמה שנים, מאזין של הפודקאסט מהונגריה, בחור בשם פטר, כתב לי מייל. הוא היה בישראל למשך שנה, ובמשך השנה הזאת יצא לנו להיפגש כמה פעמים. מאז, הוא חזר להונגריה, ובשנה שעברה כשהייתי בבודפשט יצא לנו שוב להיפגש כמה פעמים. אז השנה כמובן שנפגשנו שוב. מדי פעם, יצא לי לדבר איתו גם על הבחירות. וביום הבחירות, פטר הזמין אותי למסיבת תוצאות. כלומר, לאירוע שבו אנשים יושבים ורואים ביחד את התוצאות של הבחירות. בעצם, ב-00:20 בערב ההצבעה נגמרת והתוצאות מתחילות להגיע. אז פטר והחברים שלו תכננו להיפגש ב-00:20 בערב ולראות ביחד את התוצאות.

הבעיה היא שבדרך-כלל לתוצאות לוקח זמן להגיע. כי לוקח זמן לספור את כל ההצבעות. צריך לפעמים לחכות עד אמצע הלילה או עד הבוקר למחרת כדי לדעת מי ניצח. לפעמים אפילו יותר. אז אני לא הייתי בטוחה שזה רעיון כל-כך טוב. כי אני לא רציתי לבלות את כל הלילה במסיבת תוצאות. בכל מקרה, החלטתי שאני כן אגיע למסיבה, אשב קצת עם פטר והחברים שלו, ואחזור הביתה אחרי שעה-שעתיים.

והאמת היא שאני מאוד שמחה שזה מה שהחלטתי. כי הניצחון של מג'יאר היה כל-כך גדול שכבר בשלב די מוקדם של הערב היה ברור שהוא זה שניצח. וכבר בשלב די מוקדם של הערב אורבן יצא לתקשורת, הודה בהפסד ובירך את מג'יאר על הניצחון. ואז התחילו החגיגות הגדולות. המון אנשים בבודפשט יצאו לרחובות כדי לחגוג. וגם אנחנו היינו בחוץ, ברחוב. ראיתי מסביבי המון אנשים רוקדים ושרים ופשוט מאוד שמחים. והאמת היא שהיה בזה משהו מאוד מרגש. היה אפשר להרגיש שזה רגע היסטורי.

מאוחר יותר, בדרך הביתה, ראיתי אנשים רוקדים ושרים גם ברכבת, ובעצם אני לא חושבת שהיה מקום בבודפשט שבו אנשים לא חגגו בלילה הזה.

כשחזרתי הביתה, חשבתי לעצמי שהערב הזה היה ערב מיוחד שאני בטוח אזכור להרבה מאוד זמן.

זהו. הגענו לסוף הפרק.

זהו. תודה רבה רבה שהאזנתם והאזנתן, ואנחנו נשתמע בפעם הבאה. יאללה ביי! להתראות!

english_paragraphs: Hello everyone, and welcome to the new episode of the podcast “Hebrew Time.” If you’ve been listening to this podcast long enough, you know that from time to time my husband and I travel to Europe and stay there for a certain period of time: a month, two months, sometimes even three months.

Basically, we’re renting out our apartment in Jerusalem for this period—that is, subletting our apartment—and with the money from this sublet, we’re renting another apartment in the place we’re traveling to. In a few previous episodes, I told you about trips like these: to Berlin, to Bucharest, to Budapest, and so on and so on.

This year, at the end of January, my husband and I traveled to two places: Sinaia, which is a small town in Romania, and Budapest, which is the capital of Hungary. We were in Sinaia for about a week, and in Budapest for about two months. It was an interesting period, and that is what I actually want to tell you about in this episode.
Okay. Ready? Let’s begin!
Okay. So at the end of January this year, my husband and I flew to Romania. We flew to Bucharest, and from there we took a train to Sinaia.

Sinaia is a small town located about an hour and a half by train from Bucharest. It’s a town where there isn’t much to do, but it’s in a very beautiful area with lots of high mountains and lots of snow. So basically, most people who come to Sinaia in the winter come there to ski in its snowy mountains. And that’s also why we came to Sinaia: to ski. But that wasn’t the main reason we came to Sinaia.

Not long ago, my cousin and his wife decided that they were leaving Israel and moving to... Sinya. It was something that really surprised the whole family. They actually bought a large house in Sinya, with several floors and many rooms, and decided to turn that house into a kind of boutique hotel. They basically decided that they wanted to live in Sinya and work at running this hotel. So since that happened, they have been in Sinya, renovating this house and trying to set up their hotel.

Of course, ever since all this happened, my relatives and I wanted to travel to Sinai and visit them. Both to see them and to see their house and the hotel they are building. The time that suited everyone best was January of this year. And because January is a time when you can go skiing, we decided that this visit would also be a ski vacation. By the way, if every time I say the name “Sinaiya” you think to yourself that it sounds very similar to “Sinai,” like Mount Sinai, the place where the people of Israel received the Torah, then you’re right. Sinaiya is indeed named after Mount Sinai.

In any case, at the end of January my husband and I flew to Romania, and when we arrived in Sinaia we met my relatives. They had already rented a large villa where we could all stay together, and we joined them. At first, we thought we would all sleep at my cousin’s house with his wife. But that house was still under renovation. So we rented a house
Bigger than ours for a week, and we planned to meet them several times during that week. And besides that, the plan was to get up every morning and go skiing.

I already know how to ski. Last year, I was on a ski vacation in Sweden with a friend from Sweden. And as a child, I went skiing quite a few times, but not in the mountains, only on flat ground. My relatives also already know how to ski. They go on ski vacations from time to time. But my husband has never skied. So we thought this would be a good opportunity for him to try and learn. And he agreed to try and learn. But... the truth is that he didn’t really like it very much.

To go skiing, you have to get up early in the morning. You have to take all the heavy ski equipment and go up the mountain to the ski resort. Then you just glide over the snow from one place to another. And when it’s all over, after a few hours, you feel tired. That’s because you start early in the morning and also because skiing on snow is tiring. It’s physically hard, especially at the beginning. So you just go back home at noon and rest until evening.

My husband thought all of this was just a waste of time. It didn’t seem very logical to him that all the day’s energy was being spent on going up the mountain and gliding through the snow from one place to another. In short, he thought all this activity was unnecessary. And he didn’t really want to keep coming with us to ski after the first day.

The thing is, on a ski vacation you can’t always go skiing every morning. It depends a lot on the weather. Sometimes there are strong winds, and in that case it’s dangerous to go up to the ski resort. So in fact, on most of the days we were in Sinaia, it wasn’t possible to go skiing. Except for the first day, only on the last day were we able to go skiing again. And on that day my husband preferred just to stay home. Because we couldn’t go skiing on most of the days, we did all kinds of other things. For example, one day we went to visit a castle called “Peleș Castle.” “Castle” in English is and in Russian is so Peleș Castle

Peleș is a huge and very beautiful castle that was built for the King of Romania in the 19th century. Of course, today no one lives in this castle anymore. Today it is basically a museum that you can visit. It is truly a very beautiful and impressive place. And I recommend that you go look on YouTube for all kinds of videos that show this castle, both from the inside and from the outside.

But I hope you remember that the main purpose of this trip was neither to go skiing nor to visit Peleș Castle, but to visit my cousin and his wife. The truth is that we ended up seeing them much less than we had wanted during that week. But on one of our last days in Sinaia, we did go to dinner at their house. And it was very nice to be their guests.

Their house is actually on a mountain. On one side of the house there is a forest, and on the other side there is a very beautiful view of snow-covered mountains. The truth is that saying this view is very beautiful is almost an understatement. It is simply breathtaking. And in fact, on every floor of the house there are windows from which you can see the view. The best window is the one in the living room on the middle floor. It is a huge window, almost the size of the entire wall, and in front of it there is a sitting area and a coffee table. My cousin and his wife say that every morning they start their day in that sitting area. So it was a very nice evening. We sat in their living room, ate and drank and talked. My cousin told us stories about life in Sinaia, about the differences between Romania and Israel, about how they manage in Sinaia without knowing Romanian, and so on and so on. It really was a very nice evening.

As I already said, part of the house is still under renovation. And the hotel is only supposed to open in a few months. So I hope that in the near future we’ll get to return to Sinya and visit them again, once this house has become a real hotel.

Okay. So at the beginning of February, our week in Sinia ended. Some of my relatives decided to stay in Sinia for another week. Some of my relatives flew somewhere else. And my husband and I flew to Budapest. If you’ve been listening to this podcast long enough, you may remember that last year my husband and I were also in Budapest. Around the same time, more or less. From the end of January to the beginning of March. I told you about it in episode 92. Anyway, last year we really enjoyed Budapest. It’s a very beautiful city, not expensive, and we were quite surprised by how pleasant the winter was there. I mean, it wasn’t cold compared with other places in Europe. This year we arrived in Budapest from Sinia. And in Sinia it’s very cold. So we really felt relieved when we got to Budapest.

Last year in Budapest, we rented an apartment that was relatively far from the city center. And I thought it might actually have been nice to live closer to the city center. So this time we found an apartment that is right in the city center. And I thought that was great.
The apartment itself was, all in all, very nice. And of course, we really enjoyed its excellent location. But there was one thing that was very strange: the building.
The building was large and old. One of those large, old buildings you find in many cities in Europe. With a huge entrance door, wide stairs, and so on and so on.

The first strange thing about this building was the smell. It always smelled of smoke. That is, of cigarette smoke. The first time we entered the building, we were very surprised by the smell. And then, as we went up the stairs, we saw that the whole building was full of signs saying that smoking was prohibited. Now, that’s funny. Because I’ve never seen signs saying not to smoke inside a residential building. I thought it was simply obvious that you don’t do that. And I had never smelled such a strong smell of cigarettes inside a residential building. Again, I thought it was obvious.
It goes without saying that you פשוט don’t do that. So here there were signs saying that smoking is prohibited, and also a really strong smell of smoke.

My husband and I thought it was pretty funny. And after a few days, we said that going into that building was a bit like walking into an ashtray. An ashtray is a container into which you tap the ash from a cigarette. In English and in Russian, so ever since then, we’ve been calling that building “the Ashtray Building.”

Another strange thing about this building was the residents. I mean the people who lived in the building. In fact, during the whole month we were there, we hardly ever saw the people who lived there. We didn’t really know who our neighbors were. When we did see people, they were very different kinds of people. From time to time, we saw people who looked like foreign students. I mean students who had come to Budapest from another country. So we thought that maybe part of this building was some kind of housing for foreign students. At other times, we saw people who looked very neglected. I mean with dirty clothes and messy hair. So we thought that maybe this place had some kind of drug or alcohol rehabilitation center. Or maybe social housing for people who were in rehab.

Besides that, the people who lived in the apartment above us were completely crazy. Every night, around 12:00 or 1:00 a.m., really loud party music would start playing in their apartment. And it really sounded like there was a party going on there. Every night. Sometimes in the morning or in the afternoon, that music would start playing too. And I really don’t know what kind of people have the time or energy to party every night, or just in the middle of the day.
The truth is that, until the end, we never really found out what the story was with that building. As I said, today we just call it the “Ashtray Building.”

At the beginning of March, we were supposed to leave this apartment and return to Israel. But as you all probably remember, at the end of February a war broke out between Israel and Iran. Almost all flights were canceled, and it was very difficult to get back to the country. Not impossible, but very difficult. Maybe you remember that I told you about it in episode 109.

In any case, we were debating whether to try to go back. In the end, we decided that the best thing for us would be to rent an apartment in Budapest for another month. That is, until the beginning of April. We thought that by early April things would calm down and it would already be easier to return to the country. At first, we thought about staying in the same apartment. That is, in the ashtray building. But then we decided to at least try to see if there were other options. And indeed, we found an excellent apartment that was available exactly for the dates we needed. From the beginning of March until the beginning of April. We thought it was very strange that the apartment was available exactly for the dates we needed, because it was occupied for all the dates before and all the dates after. And דווקא during the month we needed, from the beginning of March until the beginning of April, it was completely available. Strange, right? When we arrived at the new apartment and met the landlord, he explained to us that he doesn’t rent the apartment for periods shorter than three weeks, because he doesn’t want tenants who come for a day or two and make noise and a mess. He wants calm people who come for a long period just to live normal lives.

Because, in fact, this whole area isn’t very touristy, and this building has quite a few families with children. So he only wants calm people whom he knows won’t make noise or cause trouble. And when he said that, we thought to ourselves, “Aha... that’s why the apartment was available for the whole month!”
So of course this building was nicer than the ashtray building. And the apartment itself was also nicer than the previous apartment.

Okay. In this part, I want to tell you about two more interesting things that happened to me in Budapest. The first thing I want to tell you about has to do with a climbing wall. As some of you may remember, in one of the recent episodes, episode 106, I told you that not long ago I started climbing a wall. Wall climbing is basically a kind of

Sport. We go to a place that has a special wall called a climbing wall. A climbing wall is a wall with all kinds of colorful protrusions on it, and people climb on this wall. In English, climbing a wall is, and in Russian I started climbing a wall for several reasons. First of all, I wanted to start doing some kind of sport on a regular basis. And it seemed like a nice thing to me. Besides that, I thought it could also be a good opportunity to meet new people. Because a lot of people come regularly to the climbing wall, and people who come regularly get to know one another.

Also, almost every major city in the world has a climbing wall. And that’s great. Because it was important to me that the sport I was starting to do would be one I could keep doing without any problem even when I traveled abroad. Besides, I’ve always wanted to have the chance to meet new people in the places where I am when I’m abroad. And this seemed to me like a good way to do that.
Already on the first or second day in Budapest, I found an ad on Facebook for a group that meets at a climbing wall to climb together. And I thought that was perfect, so I went.

The group was really nice. In fact, almost everyone in the group were people who weren’t exactly Hungarian, but had come to Budapest for all sorts of reasons. The group’s guide was a young man from Syria who had immigrated to Budapest a few years earlier. There was a girl from Slovakia who had come to Budapest for work. There was a guy from Azerbaijan. There was a guy from Turkey. And so on and so on.

Besides that, there was a guy working at the ticket booth. He was the one who actually sold me the ticket at the entrance. Later on, he came to climb himself. We started talking, and I found out that he was actually a Russian Jewish guy. He was born in Moscow and moved to Hungary about ten years ago. We spoke in Russian and developed a good connection. So we exchanged numbers.

By phone, and in the following two months we went climbing together a few more times. When I’m back in Budapest again, maybe this coming summer, I’m sure I’ll get in touch with him again so we can go climbing together.

Also, about a year and a half ago, a listener of the podcast sent me an email and told me a little about herself. She is a Hebrew teacher who lives in Hungary. The last time I was in Budapest, last year, we met for coffee. But we didn’t manage to meet beyond that. This time, we did manage to meet quite a few times. Why? Because we went climbing together.

So I’m very happy about all of this, because it’s exactly what I wanted when I started with this whole rock climbing thing. I wanted a sport that would be fun for me to do, that I could also do abroad, and that would also have a social aspect. That is, it would help me meet new people and stay in touch with them. That’s exactly what happened, and so I’m very happy.

Okay. The second thing I want to tell you about is related to the elections. If you follow world news, you probably know that not long ago there were elections in Hungary. Those elections were at the beginning of April. And because of the war between Israel and Iran, at the beginning of April we were still in Budapest. So it actually turned out that we were in Budapest for a long period before the elections, about two months, and also during the elections themselves. And it was very interesting to watch all of this from the sidelines.

These elections were very important. On one side was Viktor Orbán, who has been prime minister for many years. He turned Hungary into a country that opposes the European Union, even though it is still part of it. On the other side was Péter Magyar, who wanted to restore Hungary to being a country that supports the European Union.

One of the things that is well known about Orbán is that he greatly weakened democracy in Hungary. He carried out all kinds of reforms in the judicial system, the media, the electoral system, and so on and so forth. All of these things made it very difficult to defeat him in elections. Not impossible, but very difficult. Already for a long time...

For years, Orbán and his party have been becoming less and less popular in Hungary. And yet, it is very hard to beat Orbán in elections. But this time, it felt different. Péter Magyar was leading in all the polls and seemed to have a pretty good chance of winning. A few years ago, a listener of the podcast from Hungary, a guy named Péter, wrote me an email. He was in Israel for a year, and during that year we met a few times. Since then, he moved back to Hungary, and last year when I was in Budapest we got to meet a few times again. So this year, of course, we met again. From time to time, I also talked with him about the elections. And on election day, Péter invited me to a results party. That is, to an event where people sit and watch the election results together. Basically, at 12:20 a.m. the voting ends and the results start coming in. So Péter and his friends planned to meet at 12:20 a.m. and watch the results together.

The problem is that usually it takes time for the results to come in. Because it takes time to count all the votes. Sometimes you have to wait until the middle of the night or until the next morning to know who won. Sometimes even longer. So I wasn’t sure it was such a good idea. Because I didn’t want to spend the whole night at a results party. In any case, I decided that I would go to the party, sit for a while with Peter and his friends, and come home after an hour or two.

And the truth is that I’m very glad that’s what I decided. Because Magyar’s victory was so big that already fairly early in the evening it was clear that he was the one who had won. And already fairly early in the evening, Orbán went out to the media, admitted defeat, and congratulated Magyar on the victory. Then the big celebrations began. A lot of people in Budapest went out into the streets to celebrate. And we were out there too, in the street. I saw a lot of people around me dancing and singing and simply being very happy. And the truth is that there was something very moving about it. You could feel that it was a historic moment.
Later, on the way home, I saw people dancing and singing on the train as well, and in fact I don’t think there was a place in Budapest where people weren’t celebrating that night.
When I got home, I thought to myself that this evening had been a special one that I was sure I would remember for a very long time.
That’s it. We’ve reached the end of the chapter.
That’s it. Thank you so, so much for listening, and we’ll talk again next time. Bye! See you!

Basically, we’re renting out our apartment in Jerusalem for this period—that is, subletting our apartment—and with the money from this sublet, we’re renting another apartment in the place we’re traveling to. In a few previous episodes, I told you about trips like these: to Berlin, to Bucharest, to Budapest, and so on and so on.

This year, at the end of January, my husband and I traveled to two places: Sinaia, which is a small town in Romania, and Budapest, which is the capital of Hungary. We were in Sinaia for about a week, and in Budapest for about two months. It was an interesting period, and that is what I actually want to tell you about in this episode.
Okay. Ready? Let’s begin!
Okay. So at the end of January this year, my husband and I flew to Romania. We flew to Bucharest, and from there we took a train to Sinaia.

Sinaia is a small town located about an hour and a half by train from Bucharest. It’s a town where there isn’t much to do, but it’s in a very beautiful area with lots of high mountains and lots of snow. So basically, most people who come to Sinaia in the winter come there to ski in its snowy mountains. And that’s also why we came to Sinaia: to ski. But that wasn’t the main reason we came to Sinaia.

Not long ago, my cousin and his wife decided that they were leaving Israel and moving to... Sinya. It was something that really surprised the whole family. They actually bought a large house in Sinya, with several floors and many rooms, and decided to turn that house into a kind of boutique hotel. They basically decided that they wanted to live in Sinya and work at running this hotel. So since that happened, they have been in Sinya, renovating this house and trying to set up their hotel.

Of course, ever since all this happened, my relatives and I wanted to travel to Sinai and visit them. Both to see them and to see their house and the hotel they are building. The time that suited everyone best was January of this year. And because January is a time when you can go skiing, we decided that this visit would also be a ski vacation. By the way, if every time I say the name “Sinaiya” you think to yourself that it sounds very similar to “Sinai,” like Mount Sinai, the place where the people of Israel received the Torah, then you’re right. Sinaiya is indeed named after Mount Sinai.

In any case, at the end of January my husband and I flew to Romania, and when we arrived in Sinaia we met my relatives. They had already rented a large villa where we could all stay together, and we joined them. At first, we thought we would all sleep at my cousin’s house with his wife. But that house was still under renovation. So we rented a house
Bigger than ours for a week, and we planned to meet them several times during that week. And besides that, the plan was to get up every morning and go skiing.

I already know how to ski. Last year, I was on a ski vacation in Sweden with a friend from Sweden. And as a child, I went skiing quite a few times, but not in the mountains, only on flat ground. My relatives also already know how to ski. They go on ski vacations from time to time. But my husband has never skied. So we thought this would be a good opportunity for him to try and learn. And he agreed to try and learn. But... the truth is that he didn’t really like it very much.

To go skiing, you have to get up early in the morning. You have to take all the heavy ski equipment and go up the mountain to the ski resort. Then you just glide over the snow from one place to another. And when it’s all over, after a few hours, you feel tired. That’s because you start early in the morning and also because skiing on snow is tiring. It’s physically hard, especially at the beginning. So you just go back home at noon and rest until evening.

My husband thought all of this was just a waste of time. It didn’t seem very logical to him that all the day’s energy was being spent on going up the mountain and gliding through the snow from one place to another. In short, he thought all this activity was unnecessary. And he didn’t really want to keep coming with us to ski after the first day.

The thing is, on a ski vacation you can’t always go skiing every morning. It depends a lot on the weather. Sometimes there are strong winds, and in that case it’s dangerous to go up to the ski resort. So in fact, on most of the days we were in Sinaia, it wasn’t possible to go skiing. Except for the first day, only on the last day were we able to go skiing again. And on that day my husband preferred just to stay home. Because we couldn’t go skiing on most of the days, we did all kinds of other things. For example, one day we went to visit a castle called “Peleș Castle.” “Castle” in English is and in Russian is so Peleș Castle

Peleș is a huge and very beautiful castle that was built for the King of Romania in the 19th century. Of course, today no one lives in this castle anymore. Today it is basically a museum that you can visit. It is truly a very beautiful and impressive place. And I recommend that you go look on YouTube for all kinds of videos that show this castle, both from the inside and from the outside.

But I hope you remember that the main purpose of this trip was neither to go skiing nor to visit Peleș Castle, but to visit my cousin and his wife. The truth is that we ended up seeing them much less than we had wanted during that week. But on one of our last days in Sinaia, we did go to dinner at their house. And it was very nice to be their guests.

Their house is actually on a mountain. On one side of the house there is a forest, and on the other side there is a very beautiful view of snow-covered mountains. The truth is that saying this view is very beautiful is almost an understatement. It is simply breathtaking. And in fact, on every floor of the house there are windows from which you can see the view. The best window is the one in the living room on the middle floor. It is a huge window, almost the size of the entire wall, and in front of it there is a sitting area and a coffee table. My cousin and his wife say that every morning they start their day in that sitting area. So it was a very nice evening. We sat in their living room, ate and drank and talked. My cousin told us stories about life in Sinaia, about the differences between Romania and Israel, about how they manage in Sinaia without knowing Romanian, and so on and so on. It really was a very nice evening.

As I already said, part of the house is still under renovation. And the hotel is only supposed to open in a few months. So I hope that in the near future we’ll get to return to Sinya and visit them again, once this house has become a real hotel.

Okay. So at the beginning of February, our week in Sinia ended. Some of my relatives decided to stay in Sinia for another week. Some of my relatives flew somewhere else. And my husband and I flew to Budapest. If you’ve been listening to this podcast long enough, you may remember that last year my husband and I were also in Budapest. Around the same time, more or less. From the end of January to the beginning of March. I told you about it in episode 92. Anyway, last year we really enjoyed Budapest. It’s a very beautiful city, not expensive, and we were quite surprised by how pleasant the winter was there. I mean, it wasn’t cold compared with other places in Europe. This year we arrived in Budapest from Sinia. And in Sinia it’s very cold. So we really felt relieved when we got to Budapest.

Last year in Budapest, we rented an apartment that was relatively far from the city center. And I thought it might actually have been nice to live closer to the city center. So this time we found an apartment that is right in the city center. And I thought that was great.
The apartment itself was, all in all, very nice. And of course, we really enjoyed its excellent location. But there was one thing that was very strange: the building.
The building was large and old. One of those large, old buildings you find in many cities in Europe. With a huge entrance door, wide stairs, and so on and so on.

The first strange thing about this building was the smell. It always smelled of smoke. That is, of cigarette smoke. The first time we entered the building, we were very surprised by the smell. And then, as we went up the stairs, we saw that the whole building was full of signs saying that smoking was prohibited. Now, that’s funny. Because I’ve never seen signs saying not to smoke inside a residential building. I thought it was simply obvious that you don’t do that. And I had never smelled such a strong smell of cigarettes inside a residential building. Again, I thought it was obvious.
It goes without saying that you פשוט don’t do that. So here there were signs saying that smoking is prohibited, and also a really strong smell of smoke.

My husband and I thought it was pretty funny. And after a few days, we said that going into that building was a bit like walking into an ashtray. An ashtray is a container into which you tap the ash from a cigarette. In English and in Russian, so ever since then, we’ve been calling that building “the Ashtray Building.”

Another strange thing about this building was the residents. I mean the people who lived in the building. In fact, during the whole month we were there, we hardly ever saw the people who lived there. We didn’t really know who our neighbors were. When we did see people, they were very different kinds of people. From time to time, we saw people who looked like foreign students. I mean students who had come to Budapest from another country. So we thought that maybe part of this building was some kind of housing for foreign students. At other times, we saw people who looked very neglected. I mean with dirty clothes and messy hair. So we thought that maybe this place had some kind of drug or alcohol rehabilitation center. Or maybe social housing for people who were in rehab.

Besides that, the people who lived in the apartment above us were completely crazy. Every night, around 12:00 or 1:00 a.m., really loud party music would start playing in their apartment. And it really sounded like there was a party going on there. Every night. Sometimes in the morning or in the afternoon, that music would start playing too. And I really don’t know what kind of people have the time or energy to party every night, or just in the middle of the day.
The truth is that, until the end, we never really found out what the story was with that building. As I said, today we just call it the “Ashtray Building.”

At the beginning of March, we were supposed to leave this apartment and return to Israel. But as you all probably remember, at the end of February a war broke out between Israel and Iran. Almost all flights were canceled, and it was very difficult to get back to the country. Not impossible, but very difficult. Maybe you remember that I told you about it in episode 109.

In any case, we were debating whether to try to go back. In the end, we decided that the best thing for us would be to rent an apartment in Budapest for another month. That is, until the beginning of April. We thought that by early April things would calm down and it would already be easier to return to the country. At first, we thought about staying in the same apartment. That is, in the ashtray building. But then we decided to at least try to see if there were other options. And indeed, we found an excellent apartment that was available exactly for the dates we needed. From the beginning of March until the beginning of April. We thought it was very strange that the apartment was available exactly for the dates we needed, because it was occupied for all the dates before and all the dates after. And דווקא during the month we needed, from the beginning of March until the beginning of April, it was completely available. Strange, right? When we arrived at the new apartment and met the landlord, he explained to us that he doesn’t rent the apartment for periods shorter than three weeks, because he doesn’t want tenants who come for a day or two and make noise and a mess. He wants calm people who come for a long period just to live normal lives.

Because, in fact, this whole area isn’t very touristy, and this building has quite a few families with children. So he only wants calm people whom he knows won’t make noise or cause trouble. And when he said that, we thought to ourselves, “Aha... that’s why the apartment was available for the whole month!”
So of course this building was nicer than the ashtray building. And the apartment itself was also nicer than the previous apartment.

Okay. In this part, I want to tell you about two more interesting things that happened to me in Budapest. The first thing I want to tell you about has to do with a climbing wall. As some of you may remember, in one of the recent episodes, episode 106, I told you that not long ago I started climbing a wall. Wall climbing is basically a kind of

Sport. We go to a place that has a special wall called a climbing wall. A climbing wall is a wall with all kinds of colorful protrusions on it, and people climb on this wall. In English, climbing a wall is, and in Russian I started climbing a wall for several reasons. First of all, I wanted to start doing some kind of sport on a regular basis. And it seemed like a nice thing to me. Besides that, I thought it could also be a good opportunity to meet new people. Because a lot of people come regularly to the climbing wall, and people who come regularly get to know one another.

Also, almost every major city in the world has a climbing wall. And that’s great. Because it was important to me that the sport I was starting to do would be one I could keep doing without any problem even when I traveled abroad. Besides, I’ve always wanted to have the chance to meet new people in the places where I am when I’m abroad. And this seemed to me like a good way to do that.
Already on the first or second day in Budapest, I found an ad on Facebook for a group that meets at a climbing wall to climb together. And I thought that was perfect, so I went.

The group was really nice. In fact, almost everyone in the group were people who weren’t exactly Hungarian, but had come to Budapest for all sorts of reasons. The group’s guide was a young man from Syria who had immigrated to Budapest a few years earlier. There was a girl from Slovakia who had come to Budapest for work. There was a guy from Azerbaijan. There was a guy from Turkey. And so on and so on.

Besides that, there was a guy working at the ticket booth. He was the one who actually sold me the ticket at the entrance. Later on, he came to climb himself. We started talking, and I found out that he was actually a Russian Jewish guy. He was born in Moscow and moved to Hungary about ten years ago. We spoke in Russian and developed a good connection. So we exchanged numbers.

By phone, and in the following two months we went climbing together a few more times. When I’m back in Budapest again, maybe this coming summer, I’m sure I’ll get in touch with him again so we can go climbing together.

Also, about a year and a half ago, a listener of the podcast sent me an email and told me a little about herself. She is a Hebrew teacher who lives in Hungary. The last time I was in Budapest, last year, we met for coffee. But we didn’t manage to meet beyond that. This time, we did manage to meet quite a few times. Why? Because we went climbing together.

So I’m very happy about all of this, because it’s exactly what I wanted when I started with this whole rock climbing thing. I wanted a sport that would be fun for me to do, that I could also do abroad, and that would also have a social aspect. That is, it would help me meet new people and stay in touch with them. That’s exactly what happened, and so I’m very happy.

Okay. The second thing I want to tell you about is related to the elections. If you follow world news, you probably know that not long ago there were elections in Hungary. Those elections were at the beginning of April. And because of the war between Israel and Iran, at the beginning of April we were still in Budapest. So it actually turned out that we were in Budapest for a long period before the elections, about two months, and also during the elections themselves. And it was very interesting to watch all of this from the sidelines.

These elections were very important. On one side was Viktor Orbán, who has been prime minister for many years. He turned Hungary into a country that opposes the European Union, even though it is still part of it. On the other side was Péter Magyar, who wanted to restore Hungary to being a country that supports the European Union.

One of the things that is well known about Orbán is that he greatly weakened democracy in Hungary. He carried out all kinds of reforms in the judicial system, the media, the electoral system, and so on and so forth. All of these things made it very difficult to defeat him in elections. Not impossible, but very difficult. Already for a long time...

For years, Orbán and his party have been becoming less and less popular in Hungary. And yet, it is very hard to beat Orbán in elections. But this time, it felt different. Péter Magyar was leading in all the polls and seemed to have a pretty good chance of winning. A few years ago, a listener of the podcast from Hungary, a guy named Péter, wrote me an email. He was in Israel for a year, and during that year we met a few times. Since then, he moved back to Hungary, and last year when I was in Budapest we got to meet a few times again. So this year, of course, we met again. From time to time, I also talked with him about the elections. And on election day, Péter invited me to a results party. That is, to an event where people sit and watch the election results together. Basically, at 12:20 a.m. the voting ends and the results start coming in. So Péter and his friends planned to meet at 12:20 a.m. and watch the results together.

The problem is that usually it takes time for the results to come in. Because it takes time to count all the votes. Sometimes you have to wait until the middle of the night or until the next morning to know who won. Sometimes even longer. So I wasn’t sure it was such a good idea. Because I didn’t want to spend the whole night at a results party. In any case, I decided that I would go to the party, sit for a while with Peter and his friends, and come home after an hour or two.

And the truth is that I’m very glad that’s what I decided. Because Magyar’s victory was so big that already fairly early in the evening it was clear that he was the one who had won. And already fairly early in the evening, Orbán went out to the media, admitted defeat, and congratulated Magyar on the victory. Then the big celebrations began. A lot of people in Budapest went out into the streets to celebrate. And we were out there too, in the street. I saw a lot of people around me dancing and singing and simply being very happy. And the truth is that there was something very moving about it. You could feel that it was a historic moment.
Later, on the way home, I saw people dancing and singing on the train as well, and in fact I don’t think there was a place in Budapest where people weren’t celebrating that night.
When I got home, I thought to myself that this evening had been a special one that I was sure I would remember for a very long time.
That’s it. We’ve reached the end of the chapter.
That’s it. Thank you so, so much for listening, and we’ll talk again next time. Bye! See you!
